title: Ten Sweets, Four Children
statement: In how many ways can $10$ identical sweets be shared among $4$ children, if some children may get none?
insight: Line up the 10 sweets and 3 dividers: each arrangement of 13 symbols is one sharing.
redHerring: Splitting into cases by how many children get nothing.
hints: Represent a sharing as a row of sweets with dividers between children.
How many dividers do 4 children need?
Choose positions for 3 dividers among 13 slots.
solution: Each sharing corresponds to a row of 10 stars and 3 bars (the bars separate the children's shares). The count is $\binom{13}{3} = 286$.
